analysis_packet.certificate: Admissible construction must preserve the declared interface, online-only visibility, standard-library boundary, unique integer eviction outputs, and capacity safety. No score or trace evidence authorizes performance commitments. The anchor is inspectable evidence, not an obligatory design. The candidate hypothesis is admissible only as a testable direction, not as proof.
exact_actions: Treat the listed interface and normative task constraints as binding admissibility conditions.
Mark unavailable scores, traces, oracle decisions, benchmark content, and majority evidence as non-evidence rather than inferencing them.
Bind the constructive call to reject all commitments depending on unavailable evidence or prohibited evaluator visibility.
Allow the constructive call to examine the anchor and hypothesis as visible evidence while requiring independent reconciliation against the obligations.
Require the constructive call to preserve unresolved admissible design conflicts and choose one legal implementation without reinstating excluded commitments.
obligations: Exclude any hidden-trace, oracle, benchmark-path, external-library, networking, subprocess, or non-stdlib dependency.
Exclude unsupported claims that the anchor or proposed topology improves any optimization metric.
Require every returned value to be a unique integer key currently cached immediately before its eviction.
Require resident accounting and every insertion or replacement to remain within capacity_bytes, including zero, negative, and oversized inputs.
Preserve admissible conflict between inherited segmented recency/frequency behavior and disjoint single-reentry evidence windows without treating either as established fact.
Emit exactly one complete policy artifact only in the constructive call; this call must emit analysis only.
witnesses: The task requires Policy(capacity_bytes) and access(key, size, now) returning eviction keys.
The contract requires online one-access-at-a-time behavior and forbids benchmark, oracle, trace, and external-library use.
The anchor maintains resident and ghost state with bounded byte accounting, but its performance superiority is unsupported because scores are withheld.
The hypothesis asserts earlier localized correction timing, but provides no observed result establishing that effect.
The visible falsifier supplies no applicable majority or strict-median evidence.
